label: Compared world-relative, cross-world and competent-verdict moral supervenience
summary: Inspected the existing Blackburn competence-explanation edge, its dossier and related results, the anti-/realist explanatory-order independence test, naturalistic Railton/Boyd comparison and moral attitude intervention profiles. The source-backed edge explains why a competence norm is proposed; it is not an encoding of factual or modal supervenience. Added analyst within-world, cross-world and competent-verdict predicates and structural finite controls. Strong implies weak at fixed profile; two-world witnesses distinguish weak from strong and competence from moral facts, while two separately strongly supervenient moral assignments disagree over the identical selected natural profile. Rejected treating a competent-verdict rule as truthmaking, strong supervenience as a unique correct moral mapping, and any finite fixture as a model of a whole historical worldview. Provisional judgment and exact open bridges are recorded in docs/naturalistic-moral-realism.md, moral supervenience section. No source claim or root premise is established. Corpus and offline structural checks passed locally; Lean/Comparator/NanoDa verification remains subject to exact-head CI.
blocker: Applicability of the admitted situation domain, complete natural base, actual moral-fact assignments and any bridge from competence to metaphysical necessitation or from supervenience to explanatory priority remains OPEN. Next materially different test: compare the strongest naturalistic realist, non-naturalist realist and expressivist accounts with their own justified base descriptions and commitments on common moral cases; identify and test a proposed explanatory bridge without pretending their bases, truthmaking and verdict senses coincide.
